steps.prompt: Which sentence lets you see the feeling?
steps.b: Sam's pencil tapped a fast drumbeat on the desk.
steps.reveal: The first sentence tells you Sam is nervous. The second one shows it, so you feel it yourself. That's showing.

cards.title: Telling
cards.body: Telling names the feeling: happy, sad, angry, scared. It's quick, but the reader doesn't feel much.

cards.title: Showing
cards.body: Showing gives clues (actions, body language, words, details) so the reader works out the feeling on their own.

cards.title: Same feeling, two ways
cards.showing: Mia spun in circles, laughing, her backpack flying out behind her.
cards.note: The showing sentence never says "happy", but you know.

cards.title: Find the clues
cards.prompt: Tap the three words that show Leo is angry.
cards.text: Leo's face turned red. He stomped up the stairs and slammed his door.

prompts: Copy your favorite showing detail from your writing. What does it tell the reader?
When might telling be better than showing?
